REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL — Campus cleaning and janitorial services — 3-year contract
Lakeside Metropolitan University (fictional) · LMU-FM-2026-07

1. Introduction
Lakeside Metropolitan University (fictional) invites proposals for: campus cleaning and janitorial services — 3-year contract.
Scope: Daily cleaning, periodic deep cleaning, washroom hygiene and waste segregation across 14 campus buildings (approx. 61,000 m2 / 656,000 sq ft), with an option for two 12-month extensions.

2. Timetable
Clarification questions close: 2026-11-20 at 17:00
Optional site walk-through: 2026-11-24 at 10:00
Proposal submission deadline: 2026-12-04 at 12:00
Proposal validity: 120 days after the submission deadline
Planned contract start: 2027-02-01
All times are local time at the buyer's offices. Late proposals will not be considered.

3. Evaluation criteria
Proposals will be scored against the criteria and weightings below. Quality questions are scored from 0 to 5 and then weighted.
Q1 — Service delivery and quality plan — 30% — How the bidder will deliver the specification, inspect quality and fix defects.
Q2 — Staffing, training and supervision — 20% — Staffing model per building, supervision ratio, training and vetting.
Q3 — Sustainability and safe chemicals — 15% — Certified low-impact products, waste segregation and reduction of water use.
Q4 — Mobilisation and continuity — 10% — Transition plan from the incumbent and cover for absence or peaks.
P1 — Price — 25% — Total evaluated price from the price schedule, scored relative to the lowest compliant bid.

4. Documents to be returned
Bidders shall return the following documents. A proposal missing any mandatory document may be rejected as non-compliant.
- Signed form of tender (Mandatory)
- Technical proposal answering Q1 to Q4 (max 20 pages) (Mandatory)
- Completed price schedule (Mandatory)
- Proof of insurance cover (Mandatory)
- Three client references from the last 5 years (Mandatory)
- Health and safety policy and method statements (Mandatory)
- Product data sheets for cleaning chemicals (Mandatory)
- Sample staff rota for one building (Optional)

5. Instructions to bidders
Proposals shall be submitted in English through the buyer's e-procurement portal. Email submissions will not be accepted.
Questions shall be raised through the portal before the clarification deadline. Answers will be shared with all bidders without naming the bidder who asked.
Bidders shall not contact evaluators directly during the procurement. Canvassing will lead to exclusion.
The buyer is not bound to accept the lowest priced or any proposal and will not reimburse bid costs.

docs.label: Terms and conditions
pages:
TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF CONTRACT
Lakeside Metropolitan University (fictional) · LMU-FM-2026-07

1. Definitions and interpretation
In these conditions, the Buyer means the contracting authority named above and the Contractor means the successful bidder.

2. Contractor obligations
2.1 Insurance. The contractor shall hold public liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000 per occurrence and employer liability insurance as required by law.
2.2 Background checks. All staff with access to student residences shall pass a background check before deployment.

3. Commercial terms
3.1 Payment. Invoices shall be submitted monthly in arrears and will be paid within 30 days of receipt of a valid invoice.
3.2 Subcontracting. The contractor shall not subcontract any part of the services without the prior written approval of the University.

4. Termination
Either party may terminate for material breach that is not remedied within 30 days of written notice.
5. Governing law
The contract is governed by the law of the Buyer's jurisdiction.

docs.label: Technical specification
pages:
TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION
Lakeside Metropolitan University (fictional) · LMU-FM-2026-07

1. Purpose
This specification sets out the minimum requirements for: campus cleaning and janitorial services — 3-year contract. 'Shall' means a mandatory requirement; 'should' means a desirable requirement that will be considered in scoring.

2. Requirements (part 1)
2.1 Scope. The contractor shall clean all teaching rooms, offices and washrooms daily between 06:00 and 09:00, before the start of classes.
2.2 Quality. The contractor shall carry out monthly joint quality audits with the University and reach an average audit score of at least 85 out of 100.

3. Requirements (part 2)
3.1 Response time. Reactive cleaning requests (spills, washroom failures) shall be attended within 30 minutes during staffed hours.
3.2 Staffing. Each building shall have a named supervisor on site during every shift, with a supervision ratio of no more than one supervisor per 12 cleaning staff.
3.3 Training. All staff shall complete chemical handling and manual handling training before their first shift, with records available on request.

4. Requirements (part 3)
4.1 Sustainability. Cleaning chemicals shall carry a recognised ecolabel and microfibre systems shall be used to reduce water and chemical use.
4.2 Waste. The contractor shall segregate general waste, mixed recycling and food waste at source and report monthly tonnages.
4.3 Technology. The bidder should describe any digital tools used to record cleaning tasks, audits and requests in real time.

kb.title: Past proposal — Riverbend College cleaning contract
kb.text: Our quality plan combines daily self-checks by supervisors, weekly spot checks by the contract manager and monthly joint audits with the client. At Riverbend College the average joint audit score over 2025 was 88 out of 100. Defects found during an audit are fixed within 24 hours and logged.

kb.title: Reactive cleaning procedure
kb.text: Reactive requests are logged through a QR code or phone line and dispatched to the nearest cleaner on a handheld device. The target attendance time is 20 minutes during staffed hours, with escalation to the supervisor after 25 minutes.

kb.title: Staffing model and supervision
kb.text: Every site has a named supervisor per shift. Our standard ratio is one supervisor for every 10 cleaning staff, and supervisors spend at least half of each shift on the floor.

kb.title: Training matrix
kb.text: Induction covers chemical handling, manual handling, colour-coding, lone working and safeguarding. No one starts a shift before induction is signed off. Refresher training runs every 12 months and records are kept in our HR system.

kb.title: Green cleaning policy
kb.text: We use ecolabel-certified concentrates dispensed through closed dosing systems and colour-coded microfibre cloths and mops. On a typical site this cuts chemical use and water use compared with traditional mops and buckets.

kb.title: Waste segregation reporting
kb.text: Waste is segregated at source into general, mixed recycling and food streams. Monthly tonnage reports are shared with the client's sustainability team.

kb.title: Mobilisation plan template
kb.text: Our 6-week mobilisation covers staff transfer meetings, site surveys, equipment delivery, induction and a two-week shadowing period with the incumbent before go-live.

kb.title: Insurance certificate summary
kb.text: Public liability cover USD 10,000,000 per occurrence. Employer liability cover as required by law. Certificates are renewed every January.

kb.title: Digital task tracking
kb.text: Cleaners record completed tasks by scanning room QR codes. Audits, requests and completion times are visible to the client on a live dashboard.

kb.title: Vetting procedure
kb.text: Staff assigned to residential or child-facing areas complete a background check before deployment. Results are stored securely and renewed every three years.

bullets.text: Daily cleaning of teaching rooms, offices and washrooms is completed in the 06:00–09:00 window, before the start of classes.
Three-layer quality plan: supervisor self-checks, weekly contract-manager spot checks and monthly joint audits with the University.
Reactive requests are logged by QR code or phone and dispatched to the nearest cleaner, with a 20-minute target, inside the 30-minute requirement.
Tasks, audits and requests are recorded by room QR scan and shown on a live client dashboard.
A named supervisor per building per shift, at a ratio of one supervisor per 10 staff, better than the 1:12 maximum.
No one starts a shift before induction covering chemical and manual handling is signed off; refreshers every 12 months.
Background checks are completed before anyone is deployed to residences.
Ecolabel-certified concentrates through closed dosing systems, with colour-coded microfibre to cut water and chemical use.
Waste segregated at source into general, mixed recycling and food streams, with monthly tonnage reports.
A 6-week mobilisation: staff transfer meetings, site surveys, equipment delivery, induction and two weeks of shadowing before go-live.
Absence and peak cover from a trained relief pool under the same supervisors.
Every line of the price schedule is completed; rates are fixed for 12 months, then indexed as set out in the terms.
